score.band_label: Clears the wave-1 gate on its worst axis. The largest defect in the round was found by the builder, outside its own brief, diagnosed from the running page and fixed with a one-line reversal; the axis that binds is that a caster change whose named risk is temporal shipped with zero motion frames of it.

status_reasons: R1, the change with the largest blast radius, is confirmed by an arm built to overturn it. The same three Deck vistas render with byte-identical sigma0, H and camera Y in both arms and differ only in which module owns the four fog chunks: 95% opacity at 912/1414/1726 m under render/sky.js against 48/23/294 m under world/aerial.js. The Deep Marshes vista is a legible flooded forest at HEAD and a flat grey wash with a hard horizon under the model that was winning. Only one of the two draws a world.

The canopy ruling holds under an independent re-take, and the strange result the brief flagged is the instrument rather than the GPU. The hardware budget contains six SAME-CONFIGURATION repeats nobody noticed — applyArm() only ever turns flags on, so base == terrain and terrain+canopy == terrain+canopy+geology once the flags had landed in source. Those repeats measure the run's own spread at up to 1.59 ms, median 0.55 ms; the canopy delta against the pair means is -0.37 / +0.41 / +0.60 ms, and every-caster-on is -0.10 / +0.32 / +0.21 ms. R4's self-withdrawal stands and is better evidenced than the builder knew.

The gap the builder named first is now closed and the answer is favourable. On an RTX A5000 over three 90-frame walks on one scripted path, canopy-on reads 1.888 luminance oscillations per pixel per 10 frames against canopy-off 1.848, while the sub-texel set R5 declined reads 2.017 — so the instrument can see shimmer and the shipped set does not shimmer. R5 is corroborated rather than merely asserted.

The Deep Marshes bands are not shadows, and the builder's A/B could never have found their owner. With every shadow in the game off the pattern is unchanged (rho 0.990 against a 0.957 restore-control floor); hiding the water collapses it to 0.335 and removes 42% of its energy. They belong to game/src/render/water.js, whose own header records the axis-aligned lane defect its crossed-wave field was meant to remove, and they are present at eye-blackwood as well as in the Deep Marshes.

Two claims in the report do not survive recomputation and neither changes a decision: F2's headline row crosses two sites (Salt Hills' everything arm is 1,097,770 triangles, not 1,829,748), and F3's 'terrain alone 0.009%' is an arm with flagged.cast = 0.

PASS at 7 rather than higher because the round landed a change whose named risk is temporal with no motion evidence at all, and because every appearance number in it is a statistic — no human read, no Craft number, so the plan's Craft >= 7.0 row and Ruling W2's 'show the artefact as a player meets it' are unmet for this piece. The builder says both plainly.

Status is PROVISIONAL rather than PASS for two reasons that are about this critic and not about the piece, and the validator flags both. (a) CRITIC-DOCTRINE section 8 requires a critic to record its raw measurements before reading the builder's summary; my brief directed me to read the builder's status file in full first, so saw_builder_notes_before_blind is true and cannot be undone. (b) ran_every_assigned_method is false — no orbit population and no human read. The score is 7 and clears the wave-1 gate on the evidence; the provisional flag is about the order I read things in and the methods I could not run, and an orchestrator should read it that way.

biggest_gap.what: The thirteen-region height-fog result in circulation — 13 of 13 regions improved, unusable frames 9 of 13 down to 5 — was rendered through world/aerial.js's shader chunks while they were clobbering render/sky.js, and has never been re-taken under the model that ships. It is currently the headline evidence for the atmosphere and for region identity.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: It is a claim about a build that no longer exists, and the screen that produced it has now been shown to rank the two atmosphere models the wrong way round at one of three sites tested: at vista-salt-hills frame-stats.mjs gives the broken model higher edge density and a wider tonal span than the shipped one, because that camera sits 168 m up in a 340 m haze layer where a smoothstep wall lands at 294 m and reads as crisper than a Beer-Lambert ramp. The project's own rule is that a measurement is a claim about a commit rather than about the project, and this number has quietly changed commits.

remedy.action: One capture run, no source edit. Re-render the thirteen Deck region vistas at HEAD twice with tools/visual/deck.mjs at one stamped commit: once as shipped, once with sky.js's heightFog feature off (setFeature('heightFog', false) sets scene.fog.heightFalloff = 0, which degenerates the Beer-Lambert integral to the height-independent case and is the honest before-arm). Run frame-stats.mjs over both. Retire reports/w1-30f/deck/F-before and F-after and mark the 9->5 figure superseded wherever it is quoted. Separately, add a subtractive mode to tools/visual/w1-30-shadow-casters.mjs#applyArm() so an arm can write false as well as true.
remedy.acceptance: A committed pair of thirteen-vista captures at one commit sha, both rendered with render/sky.js owning THREE.ShaderChunk.fog_fragment (assert it, as tools/visual/w1-30-fog-owner-ab.mjs does), with the per-region edge_density, dominant_frac and luma span of each arm published; and a restated count of vistas flagged unusable by frame-stats.mjs in each arm. A later critic can re-measure by re-running the same two commands. The gap closes when no document in the tree quotes 9->5 without naming the commit it was taken at.

secondary_observations.what: The shader-hook collision is a class, not an incident, and its largest instance is older and bigger than this round's. Material.copy() in the vendored three r180 (game/vendor/three/three.core.js:17236) does not copy onBeforeCompile and does deep-copy userData through JSON, so every .clone() of a worldMaterial silently drops installSurfaceShader's detail-normal/wear/wetness pass while keeping userData.surfaceUniforms. Measured in the page: 305 of 406 materials carrying surfaceUniforms have a hook that no longer installs them, including actor-body:saxhleel:skin and :cloth. The mechanism arm is explicit: source hook installs surface = true, clone hook installs surface = false, clone keeps surfaceUniforms = true. Not this round's file (render/visual-foundation.js, render/actor.js).

The 1080p budget shows that no shadow-pass cost is detectable in end-to-end stepFrames(1) wall clock on an L4; it does not show the shadow pass is cheap. frameMs() times a Node-to-CDP round trip around one simulation step, the run's nvidia-smi.csv holds only the GPU identity line and never sampled utilisation, and the medians are not ordered by triangle count across sites (Blackwood 6 ms at 1.36 M caster triangles; Salt Hills 13.7 ms at 485 k). Enough to land the canopy; not enough to retire the question for weaker hardware. Remediation is two lines: sample nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu -l 1 alongside the capture, and wrap the shadow pass in EXT_disjoint_timer_query.

docs/art-direction/board.json carries 92 set targets, including FID-AERIAL-exterior_daylight and FID-SHADOWLIT-exterior_daylight — the two rows this round's subject matter lands squarely on — and no tool in tools/ reads that file. The board's own statistics are computed only over reference plates by docs/art-direction/measure-plates.mjs, and no instrument applies them to a game frame. That is RI-MTH07's exact failure shape on a corpus artefact rather than on a model: an authored target with no consumer.

tools/control-clone.mjs cannot clone tools/: it refuses the symlinks npm leaves in tools/node_modules/.bin with 'neither a regular file nor a directory (mode 120777)'. The refusal is correct behaviour and the workaround (--paths game, then --entry <clone>/game/index.html) is already used by tools/map/fog-control.mjs, but it is not in the tool's own usage text and cost this critic a detour. One line of --help would pay for itself.

vista-blackwood is confirmed as a non-instrument by an independent third measurement. A nineteen-fold change in the fog wall (912 m to 48 m) moves its dominant fraction by 0.0 points, its edge density by 0.16 and its luma span by 1. F8 and W1-30V's vista-valus-ridge finding both stand; the Deck should move that camera before any more atmosphere work is judged at it.

corpus_extended.note: RI-VIS04 §3 names 'shadows shimmer and crawl as the camera moves' as a TELL and gives it no DETECT. Every image metric in RI-VIS03 is per-frame, and the two temporal ones (M11 LOD pop, M12 TemporalVar) measure a stationary camera or an animated-region mask — neither can separate a shadow sweeping smoothly across a pixel from a shadow texel flipping, and in a forest frame a plain frame-to-frame diff scores the foliage, the camera and the defect the same. The statistic added here is the zero-crossing rate of each pixel's luminance time series over a scripted walk, counted only on swings above a threshold: a smooth ramp contributes zero reversals. It ships with a positive control (the sub-texel bucket set) so a blind instrument reddens instead of passing. Offered as a candidate DETECT for RI-VIS04 §3's third TELL.

A visible artefact on a large surface has no method in the corpus for saying WHICH mesh owns it, and 'not mine' is where three separate rounds have stopped. The pattern here: high-pass a fixed crop chosen before any arm runs, correlate each arm against an untouched baseline, and include a restore control that sets the site's own nondeterminism floor so an arm reading above it is known to have changed nothing. Two things it made possible that a caster A/B could not: proving an artefact is not a shadow at all (shadows-off rho 0.990 against a 0.957 floor) and naming its owner (water-hidden rho 0.335). Generalises to any 'is this acne / z-fighting / tiling / a shadow' question.

Nothing in the tree asserted who owns THREE.ShaderChunk or a material's onBeforeCompile, which is how two modules patched the same four chunks for four hours with both agents' controls passing. This reads both back out of the running page and fails closed, and it carries its own mechanism arm for the second shape (Material.clone() drops onBeforeCompile and keeps userData). The builder asked for exactly this and said it did not have the budget; it is 130 lines.

Every appearance claim in this verdict is therefore an instrument reading, and the two that matter most (the fog A/B and the bands ownership) are also visible directly in committed frames so a human can overrule them by looking.

method_deviations.deviation: M12's own metrics (FresnelDelta, ReflCorr, TemporalVar over 30 stationary frames, WATER_MASK) were not computed. The water finding is a band-structure correlation with a hide-the-mesh ownership arm instead.
method_deviations.why: M12 needs a hand-drawn WATER_MASK and a stationary 30-frame capture; the defect found here is a spatial lattice, which the correlation measures directly and which the ownership arm attributes without a mask. Recorded so nobody reads the water row as an M12 result.

method_deviations.deviation: Each arm was walked once. No repeatability estimate exists for the flicker statistic, which is precisely the criticism this verdict makes of the builder's frame-time budget.
method_deviations.why: Pod time. The robust part of the result is the ordering (A < B < C, monotone in sub-texel content) and the absence of any step change at B; a claim that the 6.8% C-over-B gap is significant would need the walk repeated, and this verdict does not make that claim.

source_reads.note: read in full to compare the two fog integrals; both compute the same height factor (e^-a - e^-b)/(b-a), and the difference is Gaussian-FogExp2-with-a-scale against Beer-Lambert, plus aerial's [0.08, 1] clamp
the atmosphere model, HeightFog's repurposing of fogNear/fogFar, airExtinction() and REGION_HEIGHT_FALLOFF_M
the commented installAerialPerspective() call, its comment block, and the five castShadow sites this round changed
line 1189, the heightFalloffM property, and the import order that decided the collision
applyArm() is additive-only, which is what turns two arm pairs into duplicates once the flags land in source
the offline instrument behind W1-30F's numbers; it evaluates T = exp(-(ext*scale*d)^2) with regions.json's raw extinction, neither of which is what the shipped renderer computes
Material.copy at 17236 and Texture.copy at 7346 — the mechanism behind the orphaned surface pass

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE: no orbit population and no human read, both recorded in method_deviations. On HAZARDS §0's fifth failure shape, applied to myself: the fog A/B's arms supply the region records, the terrain raster and the camera list identically, and that is the control rather than the flaw — those are the shared world both models are asked to draw, and the disputed input, the chunk owner, is read out of the page by both arms and differs between them. The shimmer arms supply the walk script identically by design and differ in a caster census each reads back off the scene graph. The bands correlation supplies the crop identically and is anchored by a negative control at 0.046 and a restore control at 0.957. Every instrument I built was shown to go red at least once: FOG-CHUNKS-SINGLE-OWNER reddens under --sabotage and against the control clone, NO-ORPHANED-SURFACE-PASS is red at HEAD with an explicit mechanism arm, INSTRUMENT-CAN-SEE-SHIMMER is the positive control for the shimmer statistic, and the bands probe's restore control sets the floor the other arms are read against. I proceeded past tools/contention.mjs's WAIT once, for the shimmer shakeout, and declared it in my status file as that tool asks.
